articles.body: When exhausting troops to defend a rebellion, is there an opportunity for the commander of an army to spend money from the treasury (with the president's permission, of course) to buy local alliances? Or does this need to be planned preempively during that presidency's turn and just not exhaust those troops for the attack, saving them for defending a looming rebelion?
articles.bodyXml:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<xml><safehtml>When exhausting troops to defend a rebellion, is there an opportunity for the commander of an army to spend money from the treasury (with the president's permission, of course) to buy local alliances? Or does this need to be planned preempively during that presidency's turn and just not exhaust those troops for the attack, saving them for defending a looming rebelion?</safehtml></xml>

articles.body: Latter option is correct. Don't attack with all forces during commander's turn and leave some to fight off rebelion or any other threat during events in India.

articles.body: Generally the commander will want to fight with local alliances and save regiments for defense. (With officers being more of a political/strength decision) since local alliances will take less of a loot cut for the level of power they provide and you guarantee you did not do nothing with them for that turn.

articles.body:
Hiring the alliances is the first step of the Commander’s turn. During Events, they have no turn.

Hence, indeed, as said above: hire in advance. (It’s often a good idea too as fending off an attack on the company gives you a trophy).
